title: ZeroStack Corp.
text: EX-10.1 2 exhibit10-1.htm EXHIBIT 10.1 ZeroStack Corp.: Exhibit 10.1 - Filed by newsfilecorp.com CONSULTING SERVICES AGREEMENT This CONSULTING SERVICES AGREEMENT (this "Agreement"), effective as of November 1, 2026 (the "Effective Date"), among ZeroStack Corp., (f/k/a Flora Growth Corp.), a corporation incorporated under the laws of Ontario, Canada (the "Company"), Dany Vaiman, in his individual capacity ("Mr. Vaiman"), and Summer 366 Holdings LLC, a Puerto Rico limited liability company that is controlled by Mr. Vaiman ("Summer 366" and, together with Mr. Vaiman, the "Contractors"). Each is a "Party" and together they are the "Parties." WHEREAS , the Contractors specialize in providing Chief Financial Officer consulting and operational related services; WHEREAS , both Summer 366 and Dany Vaiman will be providing Chief Financial Officer consulting and operational services to the Company with Dany Vaiman, in his personal capacity, continuing to serve as the Company's duly appointed and sole Chief Financial Officer; WHEREAS , the Contractors intend to provide certain eligible export services from Puerto Rico to the Company and have applied for a tax exemption grant under Act 60-2019, as amended, known as the Puerto Rico Incentives Code ("Act 60"), with Mr. Vaiman and Summer 366 as co-grantees thereunder; and WHEREAS , the Parties intend that the Services (as defined below) contemplated by this Agreement be performed in a manner consistent with the Contractors' intended operations as export service providers under Act 60, to the extent applicable. NOW, THEREFORE , in consideration of the promises contained herein and other good and valuable considerations, the receipt and sufficiency of which is hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows: 1) Term : The term begins on the Effective Date and continues for twelve years , unless earlier terminated under the Termination section (the "Term"). It renews for successive one-year periods unless a Party gives at least sixty (60) days' written notice of nonrenewal. 2) Scope of Services: The Company engages the Contractors to act as non-exclusive consultants to provide the Chief Financial Officer and consulting services specified in Schedule A (the "Services"). Schedule A may be amended from time to time to provide for additional Services and the elimination of certain Services upon the mutual agreement of the parties hereto. The Contractors will perform or cause to be performed the Services in a timely, efficient and workmanlike manner. The Contractor identified for a workstream (the "Performing Contractor") shall be responsible for its performance and entitled to its compensation. Mr. Vaiman shall be the principal individual providing the Services, including when acting through Summer 366. Mr. Vaiman does not personally guarantee Summer 366's other obligations solely by signing this Agreement. Each Contractor is responsible for its own breaches, and nothing herein shall otherwise impose joint and several liability on the Contractors. The Performing Contractor shall render the Services diligently, competently, in good faith, and with the professional care reasonably expected for comparable services. The Company may establish desired results, deliverables, budgets, reporting requirements, and reasonable deadlines, but shall not control the means and methods of performance. Any changes to the scope and compensation require the written consent of the Parties. Consulting Service Agreement Page 2 of 10 Mr. Vaiman shall remain personally involved in the material executive and advisory Services. The Performing Contractor may engage employees, subcontractors or qualified assistants at its own expense, subject to Company approval, not unreasonably withheld, before any delegation of material duties or access to confidential systems. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the Contractors shall not be obligated to, and shall not, take any action that the Company directs the Contractors to take which could reasonably be expected to result in a violation or breach of the Company's organizational documents, licenses or existing contractual agreements with other parties. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the Contractors shall not have authority to incur, assume, guarantee, or otherwise create any indebtedness, obligation, or liability on behalf of any Company, nor to take or cause any person or entity to take any action that would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on the assets, business, or financial condition of such Company; provided that nothing in this sentence shall be deemed to limit, restrict or otherwise affect any authority vested in Dany Vaiman in his capacity as Chief Financial Officer of the Company. The Contractors shall perform the Services with the reasonable skill, care, and diligence ordinarily exercised by competent independent professionals providing comparable services. No business result, financing outcome, tax benefit, or investment return is guaranteed. Only reasonable information-security, confidentiality, and site-safety requirements supplied in writing before execution and expressly accepted by the affected Contractor apply, together with later requirements mandated by applicable law. The Company may not unilaterally change compensation, scope, methods, hours, or the independent nature of the relationship through policies or directives. Subject to agreed deliverables and reasonable coordination deadlines, each Contractor controls the manner, means, sequence, working time, and staffing of its Services. The Company may assess deliverables against agreed specifications, but may not supervise day-to-day methods, prescribe working hours, require leave approval, or train the Contractors as employees. Each Contractor may serve other clients and advertise its business. Summer 366 may use Mr. Vaiman and other qualified personnel. The Contractors shall render the Services primarily at the Contractor's location of preference, but will, upon request of the Company or as necessary to perform the Services, provide the Services at the Company's offices, or such other locations as reasonably requested by the Company. Each Contractor shall ordinarily procure and maintain its own general-purpose business equipment, supplies, and workspace. The Company shall provide, at its expense, access to Company data, systems, proprietary software, and special equipment reasonably required solely for the engagement, without acquiring control over the Contractors' methods. Additional Company-specific expenditure requires reimbursement under the Expenses section. Consulting Service Agreement Page 3 of 10 The Contractors operate on their own account and are not entitled solely by reason of the Services to employee benefits, except as expressly agreed. For purposes of the ZeroStack Corp. 2022 Incentive Compensation Plan, formerly known as the Flora Growth Corp. 2022 Incentive Compensation Plan, as amended (the "Incentive Plan"), and the stock option award agreements between Mr. Vaiman and the Company governing the options granted on December 19, 2025, under the name Flora Growth Corp., and May 5, 2026, under the name of the Company and all agreements pertaining to Stock Appreciation Rights (collectively, the "Option Agreements," and the options granted thereunder, the "Options"), the Services personally performed by Mr. Vaiman, whether individually or through Summer 366, shall constitute "Continuous Service" under the Incentive Plan and the Option Agreements, including for purposes of the continued vesting and exercisability of the Options. 3) Nature of the Relationship : The Contractors will be independent contractors, and it is intended that the Contractors will act here under as such. Nothing in this Agreement will be construed as creating a relationship between the Contractors and the Company as agents and principal or as employer and employees, respectively. No taxes will be taken out of the Contractors compensation, except as required by law. The Contractors represent that they have filed or will file all of their tax returns as they have their own business and will be paying all of their taxes, as well as for any additional coverage the Contractors deem appropriate in the execution of this Agreement. The Company acknowledges and agrees that, for purposes of the Incentive Plan and the Option Agreements, including the vesting and exercisability of the options granted thereunder, services performed by Mr. Vaiman for the Company or a related entity, as defined in the Incentive Plan, in his individual capacity as a Contractor, or performed through Summer 366 pursuant to this Agreement or another authorized services arrangement, shall constitute his Continuous Service. His transition from employee or officer to Contractor, shall not, by itself, constitute a cessation or interruption of Continuous Service or trigger any forfeiture, termination of an option, or commencement of a post-termination exercise period, provided that he continues to perform such services in accordance with the applicable arrangement. The Company shall obtain any approval or determination of the Committee administering the Incentive Plan or other authorized corporate body, and execute any separate amendment to the Option Agreements required to give effect to this acknowledgment. Recognition of Continuous Service for these purposes does not alter the independent contractor relationship established herein or constitute a representation regarding the tax treatment of any option. Each Contractor shall maintain workers' accident compensation and other insurance only to the extent legally required for its own business and personnel. Evidence of coverage, or of a legally applicable exemption, shall be provided on reasonable request. No Company-discretionary insurance approval is a condition to payment for Services actually rendered. The Company remains responsible for insurance obligations imposed on it by law and for its own personnel. Each Contractor shall maintain the permits, authorizations, and professional licenses, if any, legally required for its own business and the Services it performs. Consulting Service Agreement Page 4 of 10 Each Contractor shall obtain and maintain an employer identification number and Puerto Rico Merchant's Registration Certificate to the extent required for its activities and shall provide appropriate evidence on reasonable request. Any sales and use tax treatment depends on applicable law and documented exemptions; this Agreement itself grants no exemption. Mr. Vaiman represents that he is a Canadian citizen and, as of the Effective Date, is authorized under applicable U.S. immigration law to work in the United States, including Puerto Rico, and to perform the Services in the capacities contemplated by this Agreement, both individually and through Summer 366. He shall maintain any authorization required for his performance of the Services during the Term and promptly notify the Company of any material change affecting that authorization. To the fullest extent permitted by law, the Company shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless each Contractor and its personnel against third-party claims, liabilities, and reasonable legal costs arising from Company-provided data, materials, or instructions; the Company's business or regulatory noncompliance; its breach of this Agreement; or Services lawfully performed in good faith within the agreed scope, except to the extent finally determined to result from the protected person's fraud, willful misconduct, or material breach. 4) Compensation: a) Base Fee. In consideration for the performance of the duties and provision of the Services under this Agreement, the Contractors shall be entitled to receive from the Company a fee (the "Base Fee") in an amount of US$350,000, or such other amount as determined on a reasonable basis as may be agreed upon by the Contractors and the Company from time to time, payable on a monthly basis. Of each monthly Base Fee, US$50,000 is payable to Mr. Vaiman and US$300,000 to Summer 366. Partial months are prorated by calendar days. Payment is for the agreed scope and reserved capacity, not employee attendance or a minimum number of hours. The Company's failure to request work within that scope does not reduce the Base Fee. Any increase in scope or reduction in fees requires the affected Contractor's signed agreement. Annual review shall not result in a unilateral reduction. b) Performance Bonus. For each calendar year, each Contractor shall be entitled to a target bonus of US$350,000, with a maximum bonus of US$700,000. The performance measures, weights, threshold, target and maximum achievement levels, and payout formula shall be agreed in Schedule B before the performance period begins. If the Company fails to agree or supply objective measures by that date, the target bonus is earned for that year, prorated for a partial year of Services. The Company shall not retroactively amend targets or exercise downward discretion after performance. The bonus earned is payable within sixty days after year-end, whether or not the engagement then continues. c) New Equity Compensation. In addition to the Base Fee and Performance Bonus, the Contractors shall be eligible to receive equity-based compensation for the Services, as may be agreed in writing with the Company and subject to any required corporate approvals. Any such compensation shall be awarded to the applicable Contractor pursuant to a separate stock option or other equity award agreement and shall be subject to the terms and conditions of that agreement and any other documents incorporated therein. Nothing in this Agreement shall amend, supersede, or otherwise impair the rights or obligations established under that award agreement. Consulting Service Agreement Page 5 of 10 d) Existing Equity Awards. Mr. Vaiman's rights with respect to the Options under the applicable Option Agreements and the Incentive Plan shall remain in effect, including continued vesting and exercisability based on the recognition of the Services as Continuous Service as described herein. Such rights are separate from, and shall not be limited by, any New Equity Compensation awarded as stated in this Agreement. e) Invoicing and Records. Each Contractor shall issue its own monthly invoice, identifying its Services, service period, beneficiary, and separately allocated fees, bonus, and other compensation. The Contractors shall maintain reasonable contemporaneous records of the person and capacity performing the work, location and dates of performance, deliverables, and time or other support for a reasonable allocation. These records are for substantiation and tax compliance, not employee supervision. Compensation earned as an employee, including any period of employment after relocation to Puerto Rico, remains governed by the applicable employment arrangements and applicable law. This Agreement does not retroactively convert employment services, accrued wages, employee bonuses, benefits, or employment termination entitlements into independent services income. No release from existing employment rights is given herein. 5) Taxes, Withholding and Reporting : Each Contractor is responsible for taxes legally imposed on its own income and for its own required returns and personnel obligations. The Company is responsible for its own taxes, legally required employer contributions, withholding, remittance, and information reporting. The Parties agree that payments made by the Company to the Contractors for the Services should not be subject to income tax withholding at source under the Puerto Rico Internal Revenue Code of 2011, as amended (the "Code"), to the extent the Company is not engaged in a trade or business or in the production of income in Puerto Rico. If withholding is otherwise required by applicable law, the Company shall make such withholding after giving effect to any applicable valid waiver or exemption certificate. The Company agrees to pay the amount of any sales, use, excise or similar taxes applicable to the performance of the Services, if any. 6) Expenses : The Company shall reimburse reasonable, documented out-of-pocket expenses, expenses approved in writing, and reasonable expenses necessarily incurred at its express request, including agreed travel. Approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed. Emergency expenditures reasonably necessary to prevent imminent material harm shall be reimbursed if promptly notified and documented. Reimbursement is due within fifteen (15) days after submission and is not conditional on renewal or payment of another invoice. Ordinary business overhead remains the Contractors' responsibility. 7) Termination : This Agreement may terminate only as provided below. All notices must comply with the Notices section. The Company bears the burden of establishing Cause and shall state the specific grounds and supporting facts in its notice. A disputed assertion of Cause does not permit withholding accrued compensation. a) Upon expiration of the Term following timely nonrenewal notice. Nonrenewal by the Company shall be treated as termination without Cause for the protective payments and equity treatment below. Nonrenewal initiated by the Contractors without Good Reason carries only the accrued entitlements specified below. Consulting Service Agreement Page 6 of 10 b) The Company may terminate without Cause, including for financial, economic, restructuring, or change-of-control reasons, only on at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice. It may waive Services during that notice period but must continue the Base Fee and contractual vesting through its expiration, subject to required award approvals. If it ends the relationship earlier, it shall pay the unpaid Base Fee for the balance of that notice period in addition to the separate termination payment below, without double recovery of the same notice-period fees. c) The Company may terminate for "Cause" only for the affected Contractor's willful and material breach of this Agreement that remains uncured thirty (30) days after detailed written notice, or that Contractor's fraud, embezzlement, or willful misconduct directly relating to the Services and causing material harm to the Company. A breach reasonably requiring longer to cure is not Cause if cure begins within thirty (30) days and is diligently completed within a further thirty (30) days. Good-faith professional judgment, a lawful refusal of instructions, failure to achieve business or bonus targets, disability, and a tax authority's disagreement with the structure are not Cause. Another Contractor's conduct is not imputed solely by reason of affiliation. d) Immediate termination is permitted only for non-curable fraud, embezzlement, or willful misconduct satisfying the Cause definition, supported by documented facts and detailed written notice. The Company may suspend access during a reasonable investigation but shall continue fees and contractual vesting unless and until Cause is established, subject to required award approvals. No investigation or suspension may be used to manufacture a forfeiture or postpone accrued payment. e) The Contractors may terminate for convenience on thirty (30) days' written notice, or immediately for material nonpayment continuing ten (10) business days after written demand, or for Good Reason under the procedure below. They may suspend affected Services on the same nonpayment notice without breach. "Good Reason" means, without the affected Contractor's written consent, a material reduction of agreed compensation or equity rights; a material adverse change of scope, independence, or Puerto Rico-based performance; a requirement to undertake unlawful activity or employee/officer duties as export Services; or another material Company breach. Good Reason requires notice within ninety (90) days after discovery, thirty (30) days for Company cure, and termination within thirty (30) days after the cure period ends. A termination for uncured nonpayment satisfying this procedure is for Good Reason. No Contractor must continue unlawful activity while a cure period runs. f) Accrued entitlements on every termination. Within fifteen (15) days after actual cessation of Services, the Company shall pay all unpaid Base Fees through the termination date, earned prior-period bonuses, reimbursable expenses, and other accrued cash entitlements. It shall also pay the current-year earned performance bonus prorated by calendar days of Services, within thirty (30) days after termination. Vested equity is not forfeited merely because this Agreement ends; the applicable exercise and settlement terms remain effective. These amounts are payable on resignation, Cause, expiration, death, or disability and are not conditioned on a release, transition work, return of materials, or continued engagement. No duplicate recovery is allowed for the same item. Consulting Service Agreement Page 7 of 10 g) Protected termination payment. If the Company terminates without Cause or elects nonrenewal, or the Contractors terminate for Good Reason, the Company shall, in addition to accrued entitlements and notice-period fees, pay each Contractor a lump sum equal to US$1,000,000. The payment is due within thirty (30) days after actual termination, subject only to legally required tax timing. 8) Confidentiality: Each receiving Party shall protect nonpublic business, technical, financial, personal, and proprietary information disclosed by another Party in connection with this Agreement that is identified as confidential or reasonably understood to be confidential ("Confidential Information"). This includes the Contractors' proprietary methods, pricing, business information, and tax and financial records as well as the Company's protected information. The receiving Party shall use reasonable care, at least equivalent to the care used for its own similar information, and use the information only for this engagement or to exercise or protect its rights. Confidential Information excludes information demonstrably public without breach, previously lawfully known without restriction, independently developed without use of protected information, or lawfully received from a third party without confidentiality duty. Disclosure is permitted to personnel, subcontractors, legal and financial advisers, insurers, and financing sources with a need to know and appropriate confidentiality duties; as legally compelled, with lawful advance notice and reasonable protective cooperation; and to tax, incentive, securities, immigration, and other regulators as reasonably necessary or legally required. No Party needs consent to report suspected legal violations, communicate with an authority, cooperate in an investigation, or make another protected disclosure. No provision limits any legally protected whistleblower award or requires prior notice of protected reporting. These confidentiality duties continue during the Term and for three (3) years thereafter, except that trade secrets remain protected while legally qualifying as such, and personal data remains protected as required by law. These duties do not restrict general professional skill, experience, or knowledge that does not disclose protected information. The statutory trade-secret immunity notices below remain applicable. The Contractors shall not be held criminally or civilly liable under any federal or state trade secret law for the disclosure of a trade secret that-(A) is made-(i) in confidence to a federal, state or local government official, either directly or indirectly, or to an attorney; and (ii) solely for the purpose of reporting or investigating a suspected violation of law; or (B) is made in a complaint or other document filed in a lawsuit or other proceeding, if such filing is made under seal. If the Contractors file a lawsuit for retaliation for reporting a suspected violation of law, they may disclose the trade secret to their attorney and use the trade secret information in the court proceeding if they (A) file any document containing the trade secret under seal and (B) do not disclose the trade secret except pursuant to court order. 9) Return of Materials and Intellectual Property : On termination and reasonable written request, each Party shall return or securely delete another Party's Confidential Information, except records reasonably retained for law, tax compliance, insurance, professional standards, or enforcement of rights, and routine backups not readily separable, all remaining subject to confidentiality. The Company owns its pre-existing materials. Each Contractor retains its pre-existing and independently developed tools, templates, models, methods, know-how, software, and improvements of general application ("Background Materials"). On full payment, the Company owns final deliverables created specifically for the Services, excluding Background Materials, which it may use only as embedded in those deliverables for its internal business. Consulting Service Agreement Page 8 of 10 10) Conflicts of Interest : Each Contractor shall disclose a potential or actual material conflict that would prevent lawful performance of its agreed Services or require misuse of another's Confidential Information. Providing services to another business, including a competitor, is not by itself a prohibited conflict. The Parties shall seek a reasonable information barrier, scope adjustment, or other accommodation before restricting an engagement. No exclusivity, noncompetition, no solicitation, or general duty of loyalty is created by this Agreement. Duties lawfully arising from a separate corporate office, if any, are not waived or converted into independent Services by this provision. 11) Compliance with Laws : Each Party shall comply with laws applicable to its own business and obligations under this Agreement. 12) Obligations to Others : To each Contractor's knowledge, no agreement prevents its lawful performance of the Services. Disclosed employment, officer roles, and pre-existing equity arrangements remain in effect according to their own terms unless separately amended. No Contractor shall use another person's confidential information without authority. 13) Notices All notices shall be in writing and delivered personally by nationally recognized courier with delivery confirmation, or by email to the designated addresses below. Notice is effective on actual delivery; email received after 5:00 p.m. Puerto Rico time or on a nonbusiness day is effective the next business day, provided no delivery-failure message is received. Termination, breach, and Good Reason notices shall be emailed and also delivered personally or by courier; they are effective on the earlier confirmed receipt. A Party may update its contact details by notice. "Business day" means a day other than Saturday, Sunday, or a Puerto Rico public holiday. Unless expressly specified as business days, periods are calendar days. To the Company To the Contractors Name: ZEROSTACK CORP.; Attention: Daniel Reis-Faria, CEO Postal Address: 2626 Cole Ave, Suite 300, Dallas, Texas, 75204, USA. E-mail: daniel.faria@zerostack.ai Telephone: DANY VAIMAN Postal Address: Tel: Email: SUMMER 366 HOLDINGS LLC Attention: Dany Vaiman Postal Address: Tel: Email: Consulting Service Agreement Page 9 of 10 14) Assignment: The Contractors may allocate or delegate Services between themselves as specified herein without further consent. Other assignments require consent not unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. The Company may not assign this Agreement without the Contractors' written consent and the successor's written assumption of all obligations; no assignment releases the Company without an express signed release. A merger, asset sale, or other succession shall preserve compensation and equity protections. Failure to procure assumption is a material breach and may constitute Good Reason. 15) Governing Law: This Agreement is governed by the substantive laws of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, without regard to conflicts rules, subject to applicable mandatory federal law. Nothing displaces nonwaivable rights or the governing law of a separate existing equity award, employment arrangement, or decree. Amendments to any such instrument require the approvals and formalities governing that instrument; this Agreement alone does not amend a nonparty issuer's obligations. 16) Survivorship: The Parties agree that the provisions of Sections 3, 5, 7(f), 7(g), 8, 9, and 15, as well as the Company's obligation to pay any compensation, reimbursable expenses, termination payments, or other amounts due pursuant to this Agreement, shall survive termination or expiration of this Agreement. Any other rights or obligations that by their nature are intended to survive termination or expiration shall also survive to the extent necessary to give them effect. 17) Entire Agreement: This Agreement and its completed, signed Schedules A and B contain the agreement concerning the Services. Amendments require the affected Parties' signatures and any issuer or corporate approval legally required. The Parties may sign in counterparts and by legally effective electronic signature. This Agreement does not release accrued rights or amend any existing employment agreement, equity award, or plan unless expressly stated in a separately executed amendment. 18) Binding Agreement: This Agreement shall be binding on and inure to the benefit of the Company and their successors and assigns and the Contractors and its heirs, administrators, executors, successors and assigns. 19) Severability: If any term or provision of this Agreement shall be found to be illegal or otherwise unenforceable, the same shall not invalidate the whole of this Agreement, but such term or provision shall be deemed modified to the extent necessary by the adjudication to render such term or provision enforceable, and the rights and obligations of the Parties shall be construed and enforced accordingly, preserving to the fullest extent permissible the intent and agreements of the Parties set forth in this Agreement. [ Signature page follows ] Consulting Service Agreement Page 10 of 10 IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Agreement as of the date above written. ZEROSTACK CORP. title: Strategic Storage Trust VI, Inc.
text: EX-10.1 3 sstvi-ex10_1.htm EX-10.1 EX-10.1 AMENDMENT NO. 7 TO THE SECOND AMENDED AND RESTATED LIMITED PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT OF STRATEGIC STORAGE OPERATING PARTNERSHIP VI, L.P. DESIGNATION OF SERIES G CONVERTIBLE PREFERRED PARTNERSHIP UNITS In accordance with Section 4.2 and Article 11 of the Second Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement, effective as of March 17, 2022, as amended by (i) Amendment No. 1 dated January 30, 2023, (ii) Amendment No. 2 dated May 1, 2023, (iii) Amendment No. 3 dated November 1, 2023, (iv) Amendment No. 4 dated September 19, 2024, (v) Amendment No. 5 dated August 29, 2025, and (vi) Amendment No. 6 dated September 30, 2025 (the “ Partnership Agreement ”), of Strategic Storage Operating Partnership VI, L.P. (the “ Partnership ”), the Partnership Agreement is hereby amended by this Amendment No. 7 thereto (this “ Amendment ”) to create a new series of Preferred Units designated as “Series G Convertible Preferred Units” (the “ Series G Preferred Units ”). Capitalized terms used and not otherwise defined herein shall have the meanings set forth in the Partnership Agreement. WHEREAS, Strategic Storage Trust VI, Inc. (the “ General Partner ”) has filed, on the date herewith, Articles Supplementary to create a new class of the General Partner’s preferred stock designated as the “Series G Convertible Preferred Stock” (the “ Series G Preferred Stock ”) and set forth the rights, preferences and privileges of the Series G Preferred Stock. WHEREAS, the parties hereto now desire to reflect the General Partner’s authorization and issuance of Series G Preferred Stock by creating the Series G Preferred Units and setting forth the rights, preferences and privileges of the Series G Preferred Units (and other terms and conditions of such units) under the Partnership Agreement. NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants contained herein, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which is hereby acknowledged, the parties hereto agree as follows: 1. Amendments to the Partnership Agreement a. Definitions. The following definitions from Article 1 are hereby amended and restated in their entirety, or if no such definition previously appeared, are added to Article 1: Partnership Unit means a fractional, undivided share of the Partnership Interests of all Partners issued hereunder, including Class A Units, Class P Units, Class T Units, Class W Units, Class Y Units, Class Z Units, Series B Preferred Units, Series C Preferred Units, Series D Preferred Units, Series E Preferred Units, and Series G Preferred Units. Without limitation on the authority of the General Partner as set forth in Section 4.3 hereof, the General Partner may designate any Partnership Units, when issued, as Common Units or Preferred Units, may establish any other class of Partnership Units, and may designate one or more series of any class of Partnership Units. The allocation of Partnership Units among the Partners shall be as set forth on Exhibit A , as such Exhibit may be amended from time to time. Series G Preferred Unit means a Partnership Unit having the rights, preferences, privileges, limitations, and restrictions labeled as the Series G Convertible Preferred Units described on Exhibit C below. b. The following provisions are hereby added as Exhibit C to the Partnership Agreement: In accordance with Section 4.2(a) and Article 11 of the Agreement, the Partnership has issued Preferred Units labeled as the Series G Convertible Preferred Partnership Units (the “ Series G Preferred Units ”) to the General Partner. The Series G Preferred Units shall have the following terms, rights and privileges: 1. Designation and Number . There shall be a series of Preferred Units designated as the “Series G Convertible Preferred Units”. The number of authorized Series G Preferred Units is 100,000. 2. Rank . The Series G Preferred Units will, with respect to distribution rights and rights upon liquidation, dissolution or winding up of the Partnership, rank senior to the Common Units, the Series D Preferred Units and the Series E Preferred Units (collectively, the “ Junior Units ”), and on parity with the Series B Preferred Units and any other preferred units issued from time to time, the terms of which provide that such securities rank on parity with the Series G Preferred Units with respect to distribution and redemption rights and rights upon the Partnership’s liquidation, dissolution or winding-up (the “ Parity Units ”). 3. Distributions . (a) Each holder of the then outstanding Series G Preferred Units shall be entitled to receive, when and as authorized by the General Partner and the Partnership, out of funds of the Partnership legally available for payment, cumulative preferential cash distributions at the Distribution Rate per Series G Preferred Unit. Such preferential distributions shall accrue on each outstanding Series G Preferred Unit on a daily basis, whether or not authorized or declared, and be cumulative from the first date on which each such Series G Preferred Unit is issued (the “ Original Issue Date ”), and shall be payable in arrears for the prior calendar quarter on or before the 30 th day of January, April, July and October of each year (each a “ Distribution Payment Date ”); provided, however , that if any Distribution Payment Date is not a Business Day, then the distribution which would otherwise have been payable on such Distribution Payment Date may be paid on the preceding Business Day or the following Business Day with the same force and effect as if paid on such Distribution Payment Date. Any distribution payable on the Series G Preferred Units for any partial distribution period will be computed on the basis of a 360-day year consisting of twelve 30-day months. A “ distribution period ” shall mean, with respect to the first “distribution period,” the period from and including the Original Issue Date to and including the first Distribution Payment Date, and with respect to each subsequent “distribution period,” the period from but excluding a Distribution Payment Date to and including the next succeeding Distribution Payment Date or other date as of which accrued distributions are to be calculated. Distributions will be payable to holders of Series G Preferred Units at the close of business on the applicable record date, which shall be the date designated by the General Partner for the payment of distributions that is not more than 30 nor less than 10 days prior to such Distribution Payment Date (each, a “ Distribution Record Date ”). 2 (b) No distributions on Series G Preferred Units shall be authorized by the Partnership or paid or set apart for payment by the Partnership at such time as the terms and provisions of any written agreement of the Partnership, including any agreement relating to its indebtedness, prohibit such declaration, payment or setting apart for payment or provide that such declaration, payment or setting apart for payment would constitute a breach thereof or a default thereunder, or if such declaration or payment shall be restricted or prohibited by law. (c) Notwithstanding the foregoing, distributions on the Series G Preferred Units shall accrue whether or not the terms and provisions set forth in Section 3(b) hereof at any time prohibit the current payment of distributions, whether or not the Partnership has earnings, whether or not there are funds legally available for the payment of such distributions and whether or not such distributions are authorized or declared. Accrued but unpaid distributions on the Series G Preferred Units will accumulate as of the Distribution Payment Date on which they first become payable. (d) Unless full cumulative distributions on all outstanding Series G Preferred Units for all past distribution periods have been or contemporaneously are authorized and declared and paid or authorized and declared and a sum sufficient for the payment thereof is set apart for payment, no distributions (other than distributions in Junior Units) shall be authorized and declared and paid or authorized and set apart for payment nor shall any other distribution be authorized and declared and made upon any Junior Units, nor shall any Junior Units be redeemed, purchased or otherwise acquired for any consideration (or any moneys be paid to or made available for a sinking fund for the redemption of any such Junior Units) by the Partnership (except (i) by conversion into or exchange for other Junior Units, (ii) by redemption, purchase or other acquisition of Common Units or such Junior Units made for purposes of an incentive, benefit, unit redemption program or unit purchase plan of the Partnership or any of its direct or indirect subsidiaries, (iii) for transfers, redemptions or purchases of Junior Units made in accordance with the Partnership Agreement in connection with transfers, redemptions or purchases of corresponding securities of the General Partner pursuant to the provisions of Article VI of the Articles of Incorporation and (iv) as otherwise required to preserve the General Partner’s REIT qualification). (e) When distributions are not paid in full (or a sum sufficient for such full payment is not set apart) on the Series G Preferred Units, all distributions payable on the Series G Preferred Units shall be paid pro rata based on the number of Series G Preferred Units then outstanding. (f) Any distribution payment made on the Series G Preferred Units shall first be credited against the earliest accrued but unpaid distribution due with respect to such units which remains payable. Holders of the Series G Preferred Units shall not be entitled to any distribution, whether payable in cash, property or units, in excess of full cumulative distributions on the Series G Preferred Units as described above. 4. Liquidation Preference . (a) Upon any voluntary or involuntary liquidation, dissolution or winding up of the Partnership (referred to herein as a “ Liquidation ”), the holders of the Series G Preferred Units will be entitled to be paid out of the assets of the Partnership legally available for distribution to its unitholders, in cash or property at its fair market value as determined by the General Partner, in an amount, for each outstanding Series G Preferred Unit equal to the greater of (i) the Liquidation 3 Amount (subject to proportionate adjustment in the event of a recapitalization, unit distribution, combination or other proportionate reduction or increase to the Series G Preferred Units), plus an amount equal to any accrued and unpaid distributions (whether or not accumulated or authorized and declared) to the date of payment or (ii) the amount that would have been payable had each Series G Preferred Unit been converted into a Common Unit pursuant to Section 6 hereof immediately prior to such Liquidation, in the event such Series G Preferred Unit is convertible pursuant to Section 6 at the time of such Liquidation (clauses (i) and (ii), collectively, the “ Liquidation Preference ”), before any distribution or payment is made to holders of Common Units or any Junior Units as to the distribution of assets upon a Liquidation. After payment of the full amount of the Liquidation Preference to which they are entitled, the holders of Series G Preferred Units will have no right or claim to any of the remaining assets of the Partnership. (b) In the event that, upon any Liquidation of the Partnership, the available assets of the Partnership are insufficient to pay the Liquidation Preference on all outstanding Series G Preferred Units, then the holders of Series G Preferred Units shall share ratably in any such distribution of assets in proportion to the full liquidating distributions per unit to which they would otherwise be respectively entitled. (c) For purposes of this Section 4, neither the voluntary sale, lease, exchange, transfer or conveyance (for cash, securities or other consideration) of all or substantially all of the property or assets of the Partnership to, nor the merger or consolidation or any other business combination of the Partnership with or into any other entity or the merger or consolidation of any other entity into or with the Partnership or a statutory unit exchange by the Partnership, shall be deemed to be a Liquidation. Upon a Partnership Change of Control, if the outstanding Series G Preferred Units are not redeemed, repurchased or converted as provided in Section 5 or 6 hereof, then the Partnership will cause any acquirer of the Partnership to assume the obligations set forth herein and be subject to the terms and conditions set forth herein. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if such assumption is not permitted by law, the Partnership shall take any actions under its control necessary to cause the acquirer to issue securities of the acquirer with substantially similar contractual rights as those contained herein (including the inclusion of a provision in the relevant merger or consolidation agreement requiring the acquirer to issue securities of the acquirer with substantially similar contractual rights as those contained herein). (d) In determining whether a distribution (other than upon voluntary or involuntary Liquidation), by redemption or other acquisition of equity securities of the Partnership or otherwise, is permitted under Delaware law, amounts that would be needed, if the Partnership were to be dissolved at the time of the distribution, to satisfy the preferential rights upon dissolution of holders of the Series G Preferred Units shall not be added to the Partnership’s total liabilities. (e) Written notice of any Liquidation, stating the payment date or dates when, and the place or places where, the amounts distributable in such circumstances shall be payable, shall be given by first class mail, postage prepaid, not less than 30 nor more than 60 days prior to the payment date stated therein to each record holder of the Series G Preferred Units at the respective address of such holders as the same shall appear on the unit transfer records of the Partnership. 5. Redemption and Repurchase . In connection with any redemption by the General Partner of any shares of Series G Preferred Stock pursuant to Section 5 of the Articles Supplementary, the Partnership shall redeem, on the date of such redemption, an equal number of Series G Preferred Units held by the 4 General Partner. As consideration for the redemption of such Series G Preferred Units, the Partnership shall deliver to the General Partner an amount of cash equal to the amount of cash, if any, paid to redeem the shares of Series G Preferred Stock. 6. Conversion Rights . The Series G Preferred Units are not convertible into or exchangeable for any other property or securities of the Partnership, except as provided in the Partnership Agreement and in this Section 6. In the event that any share of Series G Preferred Stock is converted into shares of any class of Common Stock pursuant to the provisions of Section 6 of the Articles Supplementary, the Partnership shall convert, on the date of such conversion, an equal number of Series G Preferred Units held by the General Partner into Common Units at the same conversion rate at which such shares of Series G Preferred Stock are convertible into such class of Common Stock. Any conversion pursuant to this Section 6 shall be effective as of the close of business on the date of conversion. 7. Status of Acquired Units . In the event any Series G Preferred Units have been redeemed or repurchased by the Partnership pursuant to Section 5 hereof or converted pursuant to Section 6 hereof, or otherwise reacquired by the Partnership, the units so redeemed, repurchased, converted or reacquired shall become unissued Preferred Units without further designation as to class or series, available for future classification or reclassification by the General Partner and issuance by the Partnership. 8. Record Holders . The Partnership and the transfer agent for the Series G Preferred Units may deem and treat the record holder of any Series G Preferred Units as the true and lawful owner thereof for all purposes, and neither the Partnership nor the transfer agent shall be affected by any notice to the contrary. 9. No Preemptive Rights . No holder of the Series G Preferred Units will, as a holder of the Series G Preferred Units, have any preemptive rights to purchase or subscribe for Common Units or any other security of the Partnership (whether now or hereafter authorized). 10. Notices to Holders . Unless otherwise provided herein or required by law, notices to holders of Series G Preferred Units provided for herein shall be mailed to such holders by first class mail, postage pre-paid, at the respective addresses as the same shall appear on the records of the Partnership. 11. Severability . If any of the preferences, or other rights, voting powers, restrictions, limitations as to distributions or other distributions, qualifications or terms or conditions of redemption or repurchase of the Series G Preferred Units are invalid, unlawful or incapable of being enforced by reason of any rule of law or public policy, then, to the extent permitted by law, all other preferences, or other rights, voting powers, restrictions, limitations as to distributions or other distributions, qualifications or terms or conditions of redemption or repurchase of the Series G Preferred Units which can be given effect without the invalid, unlawful or unenforceable preferences, or other rights, voting powers, restrictions, limitations as to distributions or other distributions, qualifications or terms or conditions of redemption or repurchase of the Series G Preferred Units shall remain in full force and effect and shall not be deemed dependent upon any invalid, unlawful or unenforceable preferences, or other rights, voting powers, restrictions, limitations as to distributions or other distributions, qualifications or terms or conditions of redemption or repurchase of the Series G Preferred Units. 12. Definitions . Capitalized terms used herein shall have the meanings set forth below or otherwise defined herein, which definitions shall apply only to the Series G Preferred Units and shall not affect the definition of such terms as used or as otherwise defined with respect to other classes or series of 5 Preferred Units or elsewhere in the Partnership Agreement. Capitalized terms not defined herein, shall have the meaning set forth elsewhere in the Partnership Agreement. “Business Day” means any day, other than a Saturday or Sunday, that is neither a legal holiday nor a day on which banking institutions in New York City are authorized or required by law, regulation or executive order to close. “Distribution Rate” means a rate of 8.85% per annum of the Liquidation Amount (subject to proportionate adjustment in the event of a unit split, unit distribution, combination or other proportionate reduction or increase to the Series G Preferred Units); provided , however , if the Series G Preferred Units have not been redeemed or repurchased in full on or prior to the Fifth Anniversary Date, such Distribution Rate shall increase at the rate of 0.75% per annum of the Liquidation Amount for the initial year after the Fifth Anniversary Date, and shall increase an additional 0.75% per annum of the Liquidation Amount each year thereafter to a maximum of 11.00% per annum of the Liquidation Amount until the tenth anniversary of the First Issuance Date, at which time the Distribution Rate shall increase 0.75% per annum of the Liquidation Amount each year thereafter until the Series G Preferred Units are redeemed or repurchased in full. “Exchange Act” means the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended. “Fifth Anniversary Date” means the fifth anniversary of the First Issuance Date. “First Issuance Date” means February 4, 2025. “Liquidation Amount” means $1,000.00 per Series G Preferred Unit. “Partnership Change of Control” means (i) a sale of all or substantially all of the direct or indirect assets of the Partnership (including by way of any reorganization, merger, consolidation or other similar transaction) or (ii) a direct or indirect acquisition of beneficial ownership of voting securities of the Partnership by another Person or “group” (within the meaning of Rules 13d-3 and 13d-5 under the Exchange Act) by means of any transaction or series of transactions (including any reorganization, merger, consolidation, joint venture, unit transfer or other similar transaction), pursuant to which the unitholders of the Partnership immediately preceding such transaction or transactions collectively own, following the consummation of such transaction or transactions, less than fifty percent (50%) of the total economic interests or total voting power of all securities of beneficial interest of the Partnership entitled to vote generally. “Person” means any individual, partnership, limited liability company, corporation, joint venture, trust or other legal entity. 2. Continuation of Partnership Agreement . The Partnership Agreement and this Amendment shall be read together and shall have the same force and effect as if the provisions of the Partnership Agreement and this Amendment were contained in one document. Any provisions of the Partnership Agreement not amended by this Amendment shall remain in full force and effect as provided in the Partnership Agreement immediately prior to the date hereof. In the event of a conflict between the provisions of this Amendment and the Partnership Agreement, the provisions of this Amendment shall control. 6 IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties hereto have executed this Amendment No. 7 to the Partnership Agreement as of the 30th day of October 2026. text: EX-10.1 2 ea031039001ex10-1.htm SETTLEMENT AND RELEASE AGREEMENT, DATED AS OF OCTOBER 28, 2026, BY AND BETWEEN ALLARITY THERAPEUTICS, INC. AND NOVARTIS PHARMA AG Exhibit 10.1 Certain personally identifiable information has been omitted from this exhibit pursuant to Item 601(a)(6) of Regulation S-K. Redacted information is indicated by the notation “[***]” SETTLEMENT AND RELEASE AGREEMENT This SETTLEMENT AND RELEASE AGREEMENT (this “ Agreement ”) is dated as of October 28, 2026, by and between Allarity Therapeutics Inc. (together with its parents, subsidiaries and affiliates, “ Allarity ”), and Novartis Pharma AG, a Swiss corporation (together with its parents, subsidiaries and affiliates, “ 3 rd Party Releasor ”). Allarity, and Releasor are each sometimes referred to herein individually as a “ Party ” and together as the “ Parties .” W I T N E S S E T H WHEREAS , Allarity has an aggregate current liability of $4,900,000 plus interest (the “Liability”) due to 3 rd Party Releasor. The Parties acknowledge the Liability arose under a License Agreement between 3 rd Party Releasor and Allarity Therapeutics Europe ApS, an affiliate of Allarity. Allarity enters into this Agreement for itself and, where applicable, on behalf of the aforementioned affiliate; and WHEREAS , 3 rd Party Releasor has agreed to accept $1,000,000 from Allarity as full payment for the Liability; NOW THEREFORE , in consideration of the mutual promises herein and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which is hereby acknowledged, the Parties hereto hereby agree as follows: 1. Settlement . As full consideration for the Liability, Allarity shall make payment of $1,000,000 to the 3 rd Party Releasor on the Agreement date, by way of bank transfer to: Beneficiary: Novartis Pharma AG Bank name: [***] Bank key: [***] Account no.: [***] IBAN: [***] SWIFT: [***] Novartis Netting ID: [***] 2. Release of Allarity . Upon receipt of payment of the consideration set forth in Section 1, 3 rd Party Releasor, for itself and any of its direct and indirect affiliates, parent corporations, subsidiaries, subdivisions, successors, predecessors, members, shareholders and assigns (collectively “ 3 rd Party Releasors ”), (a) releases, acquits and forever discharges Allarity and each of its direct and indirect affiliates, parents, subsidiaries, subdivisions, successors, predecessors, members, shareholders, and assigns, and their present and former officers, directors, legal representatives, employees, agents and attorneys, and their heirs, executors, administrators, trustees, successors and assigns (the parties so released, herein each an “ Allarity Releasee ” and collectively, the “ Allarity Releasees ”) of and from any and all causes of actions, claims, suits, liens, losses, damages, judgments, demands, liabilities, rights, obligations, costs, expenses, and attorneys’ fees of every nature, kind and description whatsoever, at law or in equity, whether individual, class or derivative in nature, whether based on federal, state or foreign law or right of action, mature or unmatured, accrued or not accrued, known or unknown, fixed or contingent, which the 3 rd Party Releasors ever had, now have or hereafter can, shall or may have against any of the Allarity Releasees in respect of the Liability (collectively, the “ Allarity Released Claim ”) and (b) covenants not to institute, maintain or prosecute any action, claim, suit, complaint, proceeding or cause of action or any kind to enforce any of the Allarity Released Claim, unless such claim relates to or arises from the Allarity Releasee’s failure to perform under this Agreement. In any litigation arising from or related to an alleged breach of this Section, this Agreement may be pleaded as a defense, counterclaim or crossclaim, and shall be admissible into evidence. Each 3 rd Party Releasor expressly covenants and agrees that the release granted by it in this Section shall be binding in all respects upon the 3 rd Party Releasors and shall inure to the benefit of the successors and assigns of the Allarity Releasees, and agrees that the Allarity Releasees shall have no further liabilities or obligations to 3 rd Party Releasors, except as provided in this Agreement. Excluded from the foregoing releases are any claims relating to or arising from the enforcement of this Agreement. 3. Release of 3 rd Party Releasor . As of the date of payment and/or delivery of the consideration items set forth in Section 1, Allarity, for itself and each of its direct and indirect affiliates, parent corporations, subsidiaries, subdivisions, successors, predecessors, members, shareholders and assigns (collectively the “ Allarity Releasors ”), hereby (a) releases, acquits and forever discharges 3 rd Party Releasor and each of its direct and indirect affiliates, parents, subsidiaries, subdivisions, successors, predecessors, members, shareholders, and assigns, and their present and former officers, directors, legal representatives, employees, agents and attorneys, and their heirs, executors, administrators, trustees, successors and assigns (the parties so released, herein each a “ 3 rd Party Releasor Releasee ” and collectively, the “ 3 rd Party Releasor Releasees ”) of and from any and all causes of actions, claims, suits, liens, losses, damages, judgments, demands, liabilities, rights, obligations, costs, expenses, and attorneys’ fees of every nature, kind and description whatsoever, at law or in equity, whether individual, class or derivative in nature, whether based on federal, state or foreign law or right of action, mature or unmatured, accrued or not accrued, known or unknown, fixed or contingent, which the Allarity Releasors ever had, now have or hereafter can, shall or may have against any 3 rd Party Releasor Releasees by reason of any matter, cause or thing whatsoever arising (collectively, the “ 3 rd Party Releasor Released Claims ”) and (b) covenants not to institute, maintain or prosecute any action, claim, suit, complaint, proceeding or cause of action or any kind to enforce any of the 3 rd Party Releasor Released Claims, unless such claim relates to or arises from 3 rd Party Releasor’s failure to perform under this Agreement. In any litigation arising from or related to an alleged breach of this Section, this Agreement may be pleaded as a defense, counterclaim or crossclaim, and shall be admissible into evidence. Each Allarity Releasor expressly covenants and agrees that the release granted by it in this Section shall be binding in all respects upon the Allarity Releasors and shall inure to the benefit of the successors and assigns of the 3 rd Party Releasor Releasees, and agrees that the 3 rd Party Releasor Releasees shall have no further liabilities or obligations to the Allarity Releasors, except as provided in this Agreement. Excluded from the foregoing releases are any claims relating to or arising from the enforcement of this Agreement. 2 4. Counterparts . This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts and by different Parties hereto on separate counterparts, each of which counterparts, when executed and delivered, shall be deemed an original and all of which counterparts, taken together, shall constitute one and the same Agreement. A facsimile or PDF signature shall be deemed to be an original signature for all purposes. 5. Further Assurances . Each Party hereto agrees that, from time to time, such Party will promptly execute and deliver all such further notices, instruments, consents and documents, and take all such further action, as may be reasonably necessary to effect the agreements of the Parties hereto set forth herein. 6. Successors and Assigns . This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of each Party hereto and its successors and assigns. The Parties acknowledge and agree that the 3 rd Party Releasees and Allarity Releasees are intended third party beneficiaries of this Agreement and that each of them may independently enforce the terms of this Agreement just as if they were parties. 7. Interpretation; Entire Agreement . This Agreement sets forth the entire agreement and understanding among the Parties relating to the subject matter of this Agreement and all prior or contemporaneous agreements, understandings, representations and settlements, oral or written, relating to the subject matter, are merged herein. This Agreement may not be altered or amended except by a written instrument signed by all of the Parties. Any provision of this Agreement is found to be contrary to law or otherwise invalid, void or unenforceable, it shall be deemed omitted but shall not affect the remaining terms of this Agreement, which shall remain in full force and effect. 8. Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed in accordance with, the internal laws of the State of New York without regard to any law or principles that would make this choice of law provision invalid. Each of the parties hereto irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the State of New York located in New York County and the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York for the purpose of any suit, action, proceeding or judgment relating to or arising out of this Agreement and the transactions contemplated hereby. Each of the parties hereto irrevocably consents to the jurisdiction of any such court in any such suit, action or proceeding and to the laying of venue in such court. Each party hereto irrevocably waives any objection to the laying of venue of any such suit, action or proceeding brought in such courts and irrevocably waives any claim that any such suit, action or proceeding brought in any such court has been brought in an inconvenient forum. 9. Authority . Each person whose signature is affixed hereto in a representative capacity represents and warrants that he or she is authorized and empowered to execute this Agreement on behalf of, and to bind, the person or entity on whose behalf his or her signature is affixed, and the Parties hereto represent and warrant that they have all requisite authority to enter into this agreement and effect the terms thereof. [Signature Page Follows] 3 Intending to be legally bound hereby, the parties executed the foregoing Settlement and Release Agreement this 28 th day of October, 2026. ALLARITY THERAPEUTICS INC. By: /s/ Thomas H. Jensen Name: Thomas H. Jensen Title: Chief Executive Officer NOVARTIS PHARMA AG By: /s/ Arne Woern Name: Arne Woern Title: Global Head Alliance Management NOVARTIS PHARMA AG By: /s/ Dalia Sarhan Name: Dalia Sarhan Title: Head Legal TA Oncology, International 4

title: Keen Vision Acquisition Corp.
text: EX-10.1 2 ea031048601ex10-1.htm PROMISSORY NOTE DATED OCTOBER 27, 2026 Exhibit 10.1 THIS NOTE HAS NOT BEEN REGISTERED UNDER THE SECURITIES ACT OF 1933, AS AMENDED (THE “SECURITIES ACT”). THIS NOTE HAS BEEN ACQUIRED FOR INVESTMENT ONLY AND MAY NOT BE SOLD, TRANSFERRED OR ASSIGNED IN THE ABSENCE OF REGISTRATION OF THE RESALE THEREOF UNDER THE SECURITIES ACT OR AN OPINION OF COUNSEL REASONABLY SATISFACTORY IN FORM, SCOPE AND SUBSTANCE TO THE COMPANY THAT SUCH REGISTRATION IS NOT REQUIRED. PROMISSORY NOTE Principal Amount: $30,000 Dated as of October 27, 2026 Keen Vision Acquisition Corporation (the “ Maker ”), promises to pay to the order of KVC Sponsor LLC or its registered assigns or successors in interest (the “ Payee ”) the principal sum of thirty thousand dollars ($30,000) in lawful money of the United States of America, on the terms and conditions described below. All payments on this Note shall be made by check or wire transfer of immediately available funds or as otherwise determined by the Maker to such account as the Payee may from time to time designate by written notice in accordance with the provisions of this Note. 1. Principal. The principal balance of this Promissory Note (this “ Note ”) shall be payable promptly after the date on which the Maker consummates an initial business combination (a “ Business Combination ”) with a target business (as described in its initial public offering prospectus dated July 24, 2023 (the “ Prospectus ”)). In the event that a Business Combination does not close on or prior to July 27, 2027, as such deadline may be further extended by the Maker, this Note shall be deemed to be terminated and no amounts will thereafter be due from Maker to Payee under the terms hereof. The principal balance may not be prepaid without the consent of the Payee. 2. Conversion Rights. The Payee has the right, but not the obligation, to convert this Note, in whole or in part, into private units (the “Units”) of the Maker, as described in the Prospectus, by providing the Maker with written notice of its intention to convert this note at least one business day prior to the closing of a Business Combination. The number of Units to be received by the Payee in connection with such conversion shall be an amount determined by dividing (x) the sum of the outstanding principal amount payable to such Payee by (y) $10.00. (a) Fractional Shares . No fractional Units will be issued upon conversion of this Note. In lieu of any fractional Units to which Payee would otherwise be entitled, Maker will pay to Payee in cash the amount of the unconverted principal balance of this note that would otherwise be converted into such fractional share. (b) Effect of Conversion . If the Maker timely receives notice of the Payee’s intention to convert this note at least one business day prior to the closing of a Business Combination, this Note shall be deemed to be converted on the date the Business Combination closes. At its expense, the Maker will, as soon as practicable after receiving this Note for cancellation after the closing of a Business Combination (assuming receipt of timely notice of conversion), issue and deliver to Payee, at Payee’s address set forth on the signature page hereto or such other address requested by Payee, a certificate or certificates for the number of Units to which Payee is entitled upon such conversion (bearing such legends as are customary pursuant to applicable state and federal securities laws), including a check payable to Payee for any cash amounts payable as a result of any fractional shares as described herein. 3. Interest. No interest shall accrue on the unpaid principal balance of this Note. 4. Application of Payments. All payments shall be applied first to payment in full of any costs incurred in the collection of any sum due under this Note, including (without limitation) reasonable attorney’s fees, then to the payment in full of any late charges and finally to the reduction of the unpaid principal balance of this Note. 5. Events of Default. The following shall constitute an event of default (“ Event of Default ”): (a) Failure to Make Required Payments. Failure by Maker to pay the principal of this Note within five (5) business days following the date when due. (b) Voluntary Liquidation, etc. The commencement by Maker of a proceeding relating to its bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, rehabilitation or other similar action, or the consent by it to the appointment of, or taking possession by, a receiver, liquidator, assignee, trustee, custodian, sequestrator (or other similar official) for Maker or for any substantial part of its property, or the making by it of any assignment for the benefit of creditors, or the failure of Maker generally to pay its debts as such debts become due, or the taking of corporate action by Maker in furtherance of any of the foregoing. (c) Involuntary Bankruptcy, etc. The entry of a decree or order for relief by a court having jurisdiction in the premises in respect of maker in an involuntary case under any applicable bankruptcy, insolvency or similar law, for the appointing of a receiver, liquidator, assignee, custodian, trustee, sequestrator (or similar official) for Maker or for any substantial part of its property, or ordering the winding-up or liquidation of the affairs of Maker, and the continuance of any such decree or order unstayed and in effect for a period of 60 consecutive days. 6. Remedies. (a) Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default specified in Section 5(a) hereof, Payee may, by written notice to Maker, declare this Note to be due immediately and payable, whereupon the unpaid principal amount of this Note, and all other amounts payable hereunder, shall become immediately due and payable without presentment, demand, protest or other notice of any kind, all of which are hereby expressly waived, anything contained herein or in the documents evidencing the same to the contrary notwithstanding. (b) Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default specified in Sections 5(b) and 5(c), the unpaid principal balance of this Note, and all other sums payable with regard to this Note, shall automatically and immediately become due and payable, in all cases without any action on the part of Payee. 7. Waivers. Maker and all endorsers and guarantors of, and sureties for, this Note waive presentment for payment, demand, notice of dishonor, protest, and notice of protest with regard to the Note, all errors, defects and imperfections in any proceedings instituted by Payee under the terms of this Note, and all benefits that might accrue to Maker by virtue of any present or future laws exempting any property, real or personal, or any part of the proceeds arising from any sale of any such property, from attachment, levy or sale under execution, or providing for any stay of execution, exemption from civil process, or extension of time for payment; and Maker agrees that any real estate that may be levied upon pursuant to a judgment obtained by virtue hereof, on any writ of execution issued hereon, may be sold upon any such writ in whole or in part in any order desired by Payee. 8. Unconditional Liability. Maker hereby waives all notices in connection with the delivery, acceptance, performance, default, or enforcement of the payment of this Note, and agrees that its liability shall be unconditional, without regard to the liability of any other party, and shall not be affected in any manner by any indulgence, extension of time, renewal, waiver or modification granted or consented to by Payee, and consents to any and all extensions of time, renewals, waivers, or modifications that may be granted by Payee with respect to the payment or other provisions of this Note, and agrees that additional makers, endorsers, guarantors, or sureties may become parties hereto without notice to Maker or affecting Maker’s liability hereunder. 9. Notices. Any notice called for hereunder shall be deemed properly given if (i) sent by certified mail, return receipt requested, (ii) personally delivered, (iii) dispatched by any form of private or governmental express mail or delivery service providing receipted delivery or (iv) sent by facsimile or (v) to the following addresses or to such other address as either party may designate by notice in accordance with this Section: If to Maker: Keen Vision Acquisition Corporation 37 Greenbriar Drive Summit NJ 07901 Attn: WONG, Kenneth K.C. If to Payee: KVC Sponsor LLC 37 Greenbriar Drive Summit NJ 07901 Attn: WONG, Kenneth K.C. 2 Notice shall be deemed given on the earlier of (i) actual receipt by the receiving party, (ii) the date shown on a facsimile transmission confirmation, (iii) the date reflected on a signed delivery receipt, or (iv) two (2) Business Days following tender of delivery or dispatch by express mail or delivery service. 10. Construction. This note shall be construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of New York, without regard to conflict of law provisions thereof. 11. Jurisdiction. The courts of New York have exclusive jurisdiction to settle any dispute arising out of or in connection with this agreement (including a dispute relating to any non- contractual obligations arising out of or in connection with this agreement) and the parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of New York. 12. Severability. Any provision contained in this Note which is prohibited or unenforceable in any jurisdiction shall, as to such jurisdiction, be ineffective to the extent of such prohibition or unenforceability without invalidating the remaining provisions hereof, and any such prohibition or unenforceability in any jurisdiction shall not invalidate or render unenforceable such provision in any other jurisdiction. 13. Trust Waiver. Payee has read the Prospectus and understands that Maker has established the trust account described in the Prospectus, initially in an amount of $151,368,750 for the benefit of the public stockholders and the underwriters of Maker’s initial public offering (the “ Underwriters ”) and that, except for certain exceptions described in the Prospectus, Maker may disburse monies from the trust account only: (i) to the public stockholders in the event of the conversion of their shares or the liquidation of Maker; or (ii) to Maker and the Underwriters after consummation of a Business Combination. Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, Payee hereby agrees that it does not have any right, title, interest or claim of any kind in or to any monies in the trust account (the “ Claim ”) and hereby waives any Claim it may have in the future as a result of, or arising out of, any negotiations, contracts or agreements with Maker and will not seek recourse against the trust account for any reason whatsoever. 14. Amendment; Waiver. Any amendment hereto or waiver of any provision hereof may be made with, and only with, the written consent of the Maker and the Payee. 15. Assignment. No assignment or transfer of this Note or any rights or obligations hereunder may be made by any party hereto (by operation of law or otherwise) without the prior written consent of the other party hereto and any attempted assignment without the required consent shall be void. 16. Further Assurance. The Maker shall, at its own cost and expense, execute and do (or procure to be executed and done by any other necessary party) all such deeds, documents, acts and things as the Payee may from time to time require as may be necessary to give full effect to this Promissory Note. 3 IN WITNESS WHEREOF, Maker, intending to be legally bound hereby, has caused this Note to be duly executed by its Chief Executive Officer the day and year first above written. Keen Vision Acquisition Corporation By: /s/ WONG, Kenneth KC Name: WONG, Kenneth KC Title: Chief Executive Officer Accepted and Agreed: KVC Sponsor LLC By: /s/ WONG, Kenneth KC Name: WONG, Kenneth KC Title: Manager 4
